beats.beat: A G Universal trades in a range of steel products including ERW pipes, MS pipes, hot and cold rolled strips and sheets, TMT bars, channels, angles, and cPVC and uPVC pipes and fittings.
The company acts as a dealer for suppliers such as Surya Roshni Limited, Jindal Supreme (India) Private Limited, Swastik Pipe Limited, Ravindra Tubes Private Limited, and Sks Ispat & Power Ltd.
A substantial portion of revenue depends on a few clients: for the period ended November 30, 2022, the top 10 clients accounted for 92.61% of sales, and the top 5 contributed more than 75%.
The company does not have long-term contracts with most customers; business is conducted on a purchase-order basis.
All revenue is domestic; the company reported no international sales in the periods shown.
The DRHP lists competitive strengths including an experienced promoter and their network, a quality policy, strengthened human capital, and existing client and supplier relationships.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations was ₹19.95 crore in FY20, ₹38.44 crore in FY21, ₹70.46 crore in FY22, and ₹34.55 crore for the 8-month period ended November 30, 2022.
Profit after tax was ₹4.95 lakh in FY20, ₹14.66 lakh in FY21, ₹70.89 lakh in FY22, and ₹114.29 lakh for the 8-month period ended November 30, 2022.
Operating profit before working capital changes was ₹7.97 lakh in FY20, ₹10.60 lakh in FY21, ₹15.43 lakh in FY22, and ₹6.60 lakh for the 8-month period ended November 30, 2022.
Net cash flow from operations was ₹19.65 lakh in FY20, ₹18.53 lakh in FY21, ₹13.47 lakh in FY22, and negative ₹22.96 lakh for the 8-month period ended November 30, 2022.
The company has not paid any dividends to date and states there is no assurance of future dividends.
No independent monitoring agency will be appointed for the issue proceeds as the issue size is less than ₹10,000 lakh.

beats.beat: The promoters are Amit Gupta (aged 48, Chairman & Managing Director) and Bharti Gupta (aged 46, Non-Executive Director). They hold 48.14% and 38.21% of the pre-issue equity respectively, totaling 86.35%.
The company's registered office is owned by Mrs. Rajesh Gupta, a relative of the promoter, and is used under a deed dated December 12, 2022.
The company has entered into related party transactions in the past and may continue to do so; the DRHP notes these may not have been on arm's length terms.
For details of legal and regulatory proceedings, the DRHP refers to a separate chapter beginning on page 191, which is not included in the provided excerpts.

beats.beat: The global steel market was valued at US$ 874.6 billion in 2021 and is expected to grow at a CAGR of 3.02% during 2022–2027.
India's crude steel production stood at 133.596 million tonnes in FY22, and finished steel consumption at 105.751 million tonnes. Exports were 13.49 MT and imports 4.67 MT.
The National Steel Policy 2017 targets 300 million tonnes of production capacity by 2030-31 and aims to raise per capita steel consumption from 74.1 kg to 160 kg.
The government approved a production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme for specialty steel in July 2021.
Demand drivers mentioned include a growing automobile sector, rising demand for long steel, and opportunities in steel recycling and urban infrastructure.
Headwinds flagged include the emergence of new COVID-19 variants, geopolitical tensions, and the climate emergency that could disrupt economic activity.

beats.beat: A G Universal Limited is a trading company that deals in steel pipes, strips, sheets and related products, acting as a distributor for several manufacturers.

The company has filed a Draft Red Herring Prospectus for an initial public offering of its equity shares on the SME platform of NSE, though the offer size and breakdown between fresh issue and offer for sale are not disclosed in the available pages.

The DRHP does not disclose the number of shares offered, the breakdown between fresh issue and offer for sale, or the stated objects of the issue in the pages provided.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: top 10 clients account for 92.61% of sales; top 5 over 75%. Loss of any major customer would materially affect revenue and profitability.
No long-term contracts with most customers; business is done on a purchase order basis, leaving revenue vulnerable to order cancellations or delays.
The prices of core products like iron and steel are subject to fluctuations due to trade policies, supply-demand shifts, and other factors beyond the company's control.
The company has not made alternate arrangements for working capital beyond existing sanctioned limits; a shortfall could disrupt operations.
Insurance coverage may not be adequate to protect against unforeseen losses.
Changes in government regulations, taxes, or political instability could harm the business.
The company does not own a registered trademark and lacks statutory protection against misuse by third parties.
No independent monitoring agency will oversee the use of issue proceeds, as the issue size is below the threshold.
